title: Wind-down plan for v1 streaming & client reconnection guidance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We will wind down the v1 streaming endpoints (SSE and legacy websocket flavors) and require clients to migrate to the unified /generate and /chat streaming variants. This ticket defines product requirements, acceptance criteria, migration guidance for SDKs and third-party clients, and the timeline for a controlled retirement. Focus areas: graceful reconnection semantics, resume tokens, idempotency, error mappings, and customer communication.
background: v1 streaming has been maintained for compatibility but prevents us from consolidating routing, improving prefix caching, and enforcing consistent backpressure semantics. Prior deprecation conversations (see dependencies) signaled the need for a deterministic migration approach to avoid client breakage and spike in support tickets.
goals: 1) Provide a clear, low-friction migration path for production clients. 2) Ensure service-level stability during and after wind-down (no regression in 95p latency or error rates). 3) Remove v1 endpoints after a 60-day grandfathering window with opt-out assistance. 4) Update SDKs and pattern guidance to handle reconnects and token expiry robustly.
out_of_scope: Changes to model families, embedding endpoints, and Dedicated capacity routing are not included here. Any on-prem private deployments will be addressed separately via Private deployment runbooks.
scope_changes: Initial scope included a simple 30-day deprecation notice. After eng review, scope expanded to include: explicit resume-token format, official SDK helper functions (JS/Python/Go) for reconnection, automated telemetry flags for migrated clients, and documented server-side compatibility window where both behaviors are supported.
acceptance_criteria: Official SDKs (JS, Python, Go) provide migration helpers and are published at >= next minor release before public deprecation notice.
No more than 1% relative increase in 5xx errors or >=5% increase in p95 latency for affected tenants during the 60-day grandfathering test window (verified via observability dashboard).
Client resume/reconnect tests exist in the integration test suite covering: mid-stream network drop, token refresh, and server-initiated rollback to non-streaming payloads.
Customer communication content (emails, Console banners, migration FAQ) approved by Legal and Support and scheduled before the public notice date.
A migration rollback plan exists: if error budgets for production customers exceed threshold, we can re-enable v1 routing for up to 72 hours while hotfixes are rolled out.
migration_steps: Step 1 (Engineering): Implement a compatibility layer in the gateway that translates v1 connect parameters to unified streaming semantics and emits a migration telemetry flag.
Step 2 (SDKs): Publish migration helpers that expose: resumeToken generation/validation, recommended reconnect backoff (jittered exponential), and idempotency key usage for resumed streams.
Step 3 (Docs): Publish a migration guide with code samples for JS/Python/Go and a checklist for production rollout.
Step 4 (Beta): Invite 10 high-usage customers to an opt-in beta with telemetry collection and proactive SE assistance.
Step 5 (Notice): Publish public deprecation announcement, Console banner, and targeted emails to customers with active v1 usage.
Step 6 (Grandfathering): 60-day window where both endpoints are served; telemetry markers used to track migration progress.
Step 7 (Disable): Disable v1 endpoints after successful gating; open a 72-hour emergency re-enable path controlled by SRE.
Step 8 (Post-mortem): Run post-release analysis and publish learnings + follow-up tickets.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout. Week 0-2: internal rollout and SDK release candidates. Week 3-6: opt-in beta with 10 customers. Week 7: public notice and start of 60-day grandfathering. Week 15: v1 disable (subject to gating). SRE will be on-call the first 10 business days after disable.
timeline_milestones: 2026-03-15: SDK RCs published and internal docs review complete
2026-03-22: Gateway compatibility layer merged behind feature flag
2026-04-01: Beta customers invited and support checklist prepared
2026-06-14: Target v1 disable date (contingent on gates)
monitoring_and_success_metrics: Define dashboard with the following key metrics: percentage of requests hitting v1 endpoints, migration_progress by customer (percent of traffic migrated), 5xx rate delta for migrated vs non-migrated traffic, p95 latency delta, number of support tickets referencing 'stream resume' or 'broken stream'. Success gates: >= 80% by-traffic migration to unified endpoints or manual approval from PM/SE before disable.
communication_plan: - Targeted emails to owners of API keys with >100K tokens/month. - Console banner and 'What's changing' doc with code snippets. - Dedicated migration FAQ and a short webinar for largest customers. - Support playbook with triage steps and escalation path to Platform SEs.
developer_notes: Resume token format: base64(prefixId || ':' || eventOffset || ':' || checksum). Keep format forward-compatible (reserve a version byte).
Backoff guidance: initial 500ms ± jitter, max 30s, use exponential factor 1.8
Idempotency: recommend idempotency-key header for resumed vs replayed streams to avoid duplicate side effects
Token refresh: allow graceful 401 with 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer refresh' semantics to prompt clients to fetch a fresh token and resume
compatibility_matrix: During the grandfathering window, the gateway will accept v1 clients and return a 'Migration-Recommended' response header. After disable, v1 connection attempts will receive 410 Gone with structured JSON explaining next steps and link to migration guide. SDKs will translate 410 into a typed MigrationRequiredError.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers on older SDKs will experience broken streams. Mitigation: send targeted emails and allow a 60-day window plus emergency re-enable for high-risk tenants.
Risk: Unexpected increase in error budgets. Mitigation: stepwise disable and SRE runbook to revert routing for specific tenants.
Risk: Confusion over resume semantics leading to duplicated application-side effects. Mitigation: recommend idempotency-keys, provide sample server-side dedupe patterns and SDK helpers.
test_plan: Add integration tests that simulate network interruptions, token rotations, and server-initiated termination. Add canary in prod routing for 1% traffic to validate gateway translations before full enablement.
approvals_required: Security review (if any tokens handling changes)
